title: Digest: Longitudinal striping in rodents
content:
Abstract
Why do some rodents exhibit longitudinal dorsal stripes rather than the much more common monochromatic pelage coloration? Caro et al. (2026) investigated this question by matching pelage patterning with socioecological variables placed on a phylogenetic tree. Their findings hint at striping being a form of predator defense that works particularly well against aerial predators, but no evidence was found for a communicative function.
